verbalization: The visible evidence suggests that Dofequidar may interact with UDP-glucuronosyltransferase 2B4 through multiple indirect pathways. The first pathway links Dofequidar to branched-chain-amino-acid aminotransferase, cytosolic, which is targeted by (-)-Mammea B/Bb, a compound that itself targets UDP-glucuronosyltransferase 2B4. The second pathway connects Dofequidar to a guanine nucleotide-binding protein G(I)/G(S)/G(O) subunit gamma-2, which is targeted by a compound (6aR,11aR)-9-hydroxy-3-methoxy-6a,11a-dihydro-6H-[1]benzofuro[3,2-c]chromene-2-carbaldehyde, which also targets UDP-glucuronosyltransferase 2B4. The third pathway shows Dofequidar targeting another compound, Abiesadine J, which in turn targets UDP-glucuronosyltransferase 2B4. These findings collectively indicate that Dofequidar may exert its effects through various molecular mechanisms that ultimately lead to the inhibition of UDP-glucuronosyltransferase 2B4. The strength of the evidence is moderate, with varying scores across the pathways, suggesting that the relationship may be mediated through different targets and pathways.
